recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants the short description to stop naming OID even as a non-exclusive example, that should be handled by a new current-scope Jira because the existing later decision supports the current source.
issue_request: FHIR-17039 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core Feed correction asking to fix the comma in the Bundle.entry.fullUrl short text and avoid implying support for bare UUID/OID values; its proposed wording was "server address or UUID-based URI" and its Jira comment records svn 14392 as the application.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git commit 7a29b021806db7f982d4826c8f6ddd8b421600fb, which changed the Bundle spreadsheet short description from "URI for resource (Absolute URL server address or UUID/OID)" to "URI for resource (Absolute URL server address or URI for UUID/OID)". That implementation clarified that UUID/OID examples were URI forms rather than bare identifiers, and the later build-source migration carried the wording into source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-16909 had just aligned the same element on URI language. Later R5 work is decisive for the current build: FHIR-31422 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and explicitly resolved that Bundle.entry.fullUrl can be an arbitrary URI, not limited to urn:uuid, urn:oid, http, and https, while adding "e.g." to the short description so UUID/OID are examples rather than restrictions. Confluence minutes show the 2021 debate over whether fullUrl was limited to HTTP/URN and record the FHIR-31422 vote; a related WGM note said a future ticket might remove OID from the short description, but no such final Jira decision was found and FHIR-31422 later resolved the ambiguity by retaining OID as one example.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Removing OID from the current Bundle.entry.fullUrl short text would conflict with the later published arbitrary-URI clarification, and the current wording no longer implies bare UUID/OID values.

related_jiras.note: Earlier STU3 fullUrl issue changed the element wording toward URI rather than URL terminology.
2021 Bundle clarification minutes mentioned a possible future OID short-description ticket, but the issue itself concerned fullUrl omission/reference-resolution text.
Published R5 decision explicitly clarified that Bundle.entry.fullUrl can be arbitrary URI and is not limited to urn:uuid, urn:oid, http, and https.
Related Bundle reference-resolution work supplied the algorithm context cited by later fullUrl issues.
